## Topic

a visualization for "How communication apprehension and publication transportation ride share differ by country"

## Method

1.  we use violin plot to visualize

2.  add 12 columns for CA

3.  add 4 columns for PTRS(public transportation ride share)

## workflow for generating the photo

import three .csv files 
```{python}
import pandas as pd

df_a = pd.read_csv("PRCAProlificExport_FileA.csv")
df_b = pd.read_csv("PRCAProlificExport_FileB.csv")
df_c = pd.read_csv("PRCAQualtricsExport_FileC.csv")

# stick df_a and df_b
df_1 = pd.concat([df_a, df_b], ignore_index=True)
print(df_1)
```

```{python}
# Merge the result with df_c using Q0 and participant id
df = pd.merge(
    df_1,
    df_c,
    left_on="Participant id",
    right_on="Q0",
    how="inner"
)

print(df.head())
```

save the merged file
```{python}
df.to_csv("merged_file.csv", index=False)
```

read into the merged file
```{python}
df = pd.read_csv("merged_file.csv")
```

```{python}
## then code into numbers:

agree_scale = {
    "Strongly disagree": 1,
    "Somewhat disagree": 2,
    "Neither agree nor disagree": 3,
    "Somewhat agree": 4,
    "Strongly agree": 5
}


reverse_agree_scale = {
    "Strongly disagree": 5,
    "Somewhat disagree": 4,
    "Neither agree nor disagree": 3,
    "Somewhat agree": 2,
    "Strongly agree": 1
}

# Coding for Q26 and Q28
frequency_scale = {
    "Never": 1,
    "0-1 days a month": 2,
    "2-4 days a month": 3,
    "4-8 days a month": 4,
    "8 or more days a month": 5
}

#
scale_d = {
    "1-2 rides in a typical day": 1,
    "3-4 rides in a typical day": 2,
    "5-6 rides in a typical day": 3,
    "7 or more rides in a typical day": 4
}

# Columns using the normal agreement scale
normal_cols = ["Q1", "Q3", "Q5", "Q13", "Q15", "Q18"]

# Columns using the reverse agreement scale
reverse_cols = ["Q2", "Q4", "Q6", "Q14", "Q16", "Q17"]

cols_c = ["Q26", "Q28"]

cols_d = ["Q27", "Q29"] 

# Apply coding
df[normal_cols] = df[normal_cols].replace(agree_scale)
df[reverse_cols] = df[reverse_cols].replace(reverse_agree_scale)
df[cols_c] = df[cols_c].replace(frequency_scale)
df[cols_d] = df[cols_d].replace(scale_d)
```


```{python}
df.head()
```


```{python}
df["sum"] = (
    df[normal_cols].sum(axis=1) +
    df[reverse_cols].sum(axis=1)
)

df["PTRS"] = (
    df[["Q26", "Q28"]].sum(axis=1) +
    df[["Q27", "Q29"]].sum(axis=1)
)
```

```{python}
df.head()
```


```{python}
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
```

```{python}
plot_df = df.melt(
    id_vars="Country of residence",
    value_vars=["sum", "PTRS"],
    var_name="Score Type",
    value_name="Score"
)

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))

sns.violinplot(
    data=plot_df,
    y="Country of residence",
    x="Score",
    hue="Score Type",
    split=False,
    inner="box"
)

plt.title("How CA and PTRS Differ by Country of Residence")
plt.ylabel("Country of residence")
plt.xlabel("Score")

plt.legend(title="Measure")
plt.tight_layout()


plt.savefig("figure.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()
```

use only the first 4 countries
```{python}
countries_to_keep = [
    "United States",
    "United Kingdom",
    "Ireland",
    "Canada"
]

plot_df_filtered = plot_df[
    plot_df["Country of residence"].isin(countries_to_keep)
]
```

```{python}
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))

sns.violinplot(
    data=plot_df_filtered,
    y="Country of residence",
    x="Score",
    hue="Score Type",
    split=False,
    inner="box"
)

plt.title("How CA and PTRS Differ by Country of Residence")
plt.ylabel("Country of residence")
plt.xlabel("Score")

plt.legend(title="Measure")
plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig("figure_top4_countries.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")

plt.show()
```
